clue.text: Lack of equivalence around society on Sabbath

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one word encloses another
in an across clue, sitting on something means being placed directly next to it in sequence

blocks.note: S is a standard abbreviation for Sabbath
parity is equality or equivalence
S is the usual abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Someone complains that society treats people unequally on the day of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lack of equivalence' reads as one phrase meaning inequality, but 'Lack' alone is the definition and 'of' merely joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsity is thinness or scarcity, and a scarcity of something is a lack of it.

clue.text: Land deal to smuggle 500 diamonds

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying goods hidden inside something, so letters are tucked within another word

blocks.note: a sale is a deal or transaction
D is the Roman numeral for 500
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A property deal is used as cover for smuggling diamonds worth five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a noun meaning ground or property, but it is a verb, as in being landed with a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: To land someone with a chore and to saddle them with it both mean to burden them with something unwelcome.

clue.text: Permission unchanged during delivery?

blocks.note: first meaning: agreement or consent
second, cryptic meaning: split as two words, something that arrives untouched is exactly as it was dispatched

explanation.surface: Consent passed along a chain of messengers without being altered on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AS SENT: a parcel that is unchanged in transit arrives as sent. The question mark flags that this second reading is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal agreement or consent, the giving of approval to a proposal or request.

clue.text: Location of flight from distant hotspot satisfactory, crossing India

indicators.note: a line crossing something passes through its middle, so one letter is placed inside the other word

blocks.note: a star is a ball of burning gas, seen from far off
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
all is well means things are satisfactory

explanation.surface: An airline route from a faraway holiday hotspot via India is reported as fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an aeroplane journey, but it is a flight of stairs, and its location is the shaft it climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical shaft in a building that houses a staircase, which is a flight of steps.

clue.text: Couple of spivs oddly supporting root's consumption

indicators.note: oddly means taking only the letters in odd-numbered places, skipping each even one
in a down clue, whatever supports something sits underneath it, so comes after it

blocks.note: a tuber is a swollen underground root, like a potato
the first, third, fifth and every other letter of these three words

explanation.surface: Two black-market dealers prop up a root vegetable's sales and eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like it means two, but its letters join those of the next two words as fodder. Consumption is the old name for the lung disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumption was the common historical name for pulmonary tuberculosis, because the illness seemed to waste the body away.

clue.text: Plan finesse in clubs, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word it governs

blocks.note: tact is delicacy or finesse in dealing with people
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A bridge player plans to lead into a finesse in the club suit early in the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a finesse is a card-play manoeuvre, which makes 'in clubs' look like part of the card picture, but those words only supply two initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre or scheme for achieving a particular goal.

clue.text: Saying a mild oath from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards runs the letters backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
egad is an old-fashioned mild exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone utters a gentle curse with a southern accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saying' reads as a verb for speaking the oath, but it is a noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional proverb or maxim, a short memorable saying expressing a general truth.

clue.text: American tour diary of composer wearing dress

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is enclosed by them, so a word sits inside another

blocks.note: to tog is to dress, as in togged up
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A composer, in a frock, keeps a journal of a concert tour of the States.
explanation.walkthrough: TOG is a British informal verb meaning to dress up. The American spelling with a single ending is why the definition says American.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelog, US spelling of travelogue, is a written or filmed account of someone's journeys.

clue.text: Sit up in pursuit, getting reprimand

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards
placed in means put inside another word

blocks.note: a chase is a pursuit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog chasing something is told off and made to sit up and beg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit up' reads as a command to straighten your posture, but it is the word itself turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise someone is to rebuke or scold them severely, the same as a reprimand.

clue.text: Dutch and American-Chinese live in Asian capital

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch
US for American
the Han are China's majority ethnic group
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A Dutch person and a Chinese-American settle down to live in an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'American-Chinese' makes it look like one nationality, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dushanbe is the capital city of Tajikistan, a country in Central Asia.

clue.text: Revolutionary had an accident touring country

indicators.note: a tour passes through places, so the answer is found running through these words
a revolution turns something right round, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter crashed while travelling around a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel such as Che, but it only signals that the letters run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a North American nation, the second largest country in the world by area.

clue.text: Rugby player in ecstasy in hospital toilets?

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter goes within the rest

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
loos are toilets, and toilets in a hospital are provided for a ward

explanation.surface: A rugby player is found high on drugs in the toilets of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: hospital toilets are LOOS FOR WARD, and the E sits after the first word. A loo is a British toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose forward is a rugby union position, the flankers and number eight in the back row of the scrum.

clue.text: Persist, wanting good make-up

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the word

blocks.note: to linger is to persist or stay on
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going despite being short of decent cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting good make-up' reads as desiring cosmetics, but 'wanting' means without and 'make-up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Liner, short for eyeliner or lip liner, is a cosmetic used to outline the eyes or lips.

clue.text: Resolve to corrupt wartime leader

indicators.note: corrupt means spoil or distort, so the letters are twisted out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A determination to bring down a leader in time of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like a verb with 'Resolve to' before it, as if someone resolves to corrupt a leader; it is the anagram signal instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin D Roosevelt was US president through most of the Second World War, so he led a nation in wartime.

clue.text: Possible pick-up points on crusades to empty planes

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only its outermost letters

blocks.note: RE means on or about, as in a letter heading
a crusade is a quest or campaign
taken as written
only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Points on crusading journeys where aircraft are emptied of passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: A request stop is a British bus stop where the bus halts only if a passenger signals, so a pick-up there is only possible.
explanation.definitionFit: At a request stop the bus collects passengers only when someone hails it, so a pick-up may or may not happen.

clue.text: Fibre from sample is hot, surprisingly

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not in the expected form, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A dietary fibre test turns out unexpectedly spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fibre' suggests roughage in food, which the sample and heat reinforce; here it is a plant fibre used for rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal hemp is the tough plant fibre from agave leaves, used to make rope and twine.

clue.text: Excitedly kiss and stroke Pole in the snow

indicators.note: done excitedly, things get agitated and jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a tick is a stroke of the pen marking something correct

explanation.surface: A romantic moment with a Polish lover out in the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Pole' look like a person from Poland, and 'stroke' looks like a caress; the pole is a staff planted in snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski stick is the pole a skier carries in each hand to push off and keep balance on the slope.

clue.text: Tottered as partially fermented grape juice drained

blocks.note: stum is unfermented or partly fermented grape juice
to bleed something is to drain liquid from it

explanation.surface: Someone wobbled about after draining a glass of half-made wine.
explanation.walkthrough: STUM is an obscure winemaking word worth learning, since setters use it. 'Partially' looks like an instruction to take part of a word, but it belongs to the definition of the juice.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to trip or walk unsteadily, like someone who tottered on their feet.

clue.text: Case of water heater cool

blocks.note: a kettle heats water
offish means aloof or cool in manner

explanation.surface: A boiler's casing that stays cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'of' in the surface looks like part of the answer phrase, but it merely joins the definition; the answer's OF comes from the start of OFFISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle of fish is an idiom for a state of affairs or situation, especially an awkward one, so a matter or case.

clue.text: Eccles is, more's the pity, returning sausage

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way one went, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Eccles is the setter, so in his own voice Eccles is becomes I am, shortened
alas and more's the pity both express regret

explanation.surface: The setter sadly admits to being, of all things, a sausage on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is the name of this puzzle's setter, so his name stands for the first person. Eccles is also a Lancashire town known for its cakes, which tempts a food reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, highly seasoned Italian sausage, usually eaten cold in slices.

clue.text: Witchdoctor's fake article

blocks.note: a sham is a fake or fraud
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A witch doctor's charms or potions are bogus goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes it look like possession, but 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a healer or priest believed to deal with spirits, much as a witch doctor is.

clue.text: "More limes!" snarled waiter

indicators.note: a snarled line is tangled, so the letters are knotted into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumpy waiter growls when a customer demands extra limes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarled' reads as how the waiter spoke, but it means tangled and works on the quoted words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is the wine waiter in a restaurant, who advises on and serves the wine.

clue.text: Pint lacking head? That is strange

indicators.note: without a head means the front letter is taken off

blocks.note: a pint is a glass of beer
i.e. is the abbreviation of the Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A drinker is puzzled that their pint has no froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the foam on a beer, which suits the picture, but it means the first letter. In Britain a pint by default means a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means uncanny or strange in a frightening, unsettling way.

clue.text: Lead hammer consumes energy

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so one word swallows a letter

blocks.note: to lash is to beat or hammer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lead-headed mallet uses up a lot of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the heavy metal describing the hammer, but it is the strap used for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's lead and a leash are the same thing, the strap or cord used to restrain an animal.

clue.text: Prime characters in tiddliest prison: lazy individuals

indicators.note: prime characters are those standing at prime-numbered positions in the string

blocks.note: the letters in positions two, three, five, seven, eleven and thirteen

explanation.surface: The smallest jail houses the laziest inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like it means best or first, but it means the positions numbered by prime numbers; the first letter is skipped because one is not prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlers are people who avoid work and waste time, so they are lazy people.

clue.text: Mug tree that encapsulates my exasperation

blocks.note: mug is slang for face
a palm is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: A kitchen stand for hanging cups somehow sums up the setter's frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug tree' is a single household object, a stand for hanging cups, so the two words must be split to give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A facepalm, slapping a hand to the forehead, is a gesture that conveys dismay or irritation in one movement.

clue.text: Child recalled desire for offal

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a kid is a child
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A child remembers craving organ meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reads as remembered, but it means turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidney is one of the internal organs eaten as offal, as in steak and kidney pie.

clue.text: Notice possibility for fostering

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, short for advertisement
an option is a possible choice

explanation.surface: An advert offers a chance to take in a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb meaning to spot something, but it is the noun, a printed announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: Fostering, in the sense of taking up and encouraging, is close to adoption, as in fostering or adopting an idea or a child.
